question.knowledge_point: Solving Inequalities Requiring Division by a Positive Factor
question.worked_solution:
First, we move all terms to the left-hand side and factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}6{x}^{5}+18x & >3x \\ 6{x}^{5}+15x & >0 \\ 3x(2{x}^{4}+5) & >0\end{aligned}
$$

Since $2{x}^{4}+5$ is always positive, we can divide both sides of the inequality by this quantity. By doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x(2{x}^{4}+5)}{2{x}^{4}+5} & >\frac{0}{2{x}^{4}+5} \\ 3x & >0 \\ x & >0.\end{aligned}
$$
